args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM

Privileged and Confidential — Attorney Work Product
Prepared for: Energy & Natural Resources Deal Team
Matter: Concession Agreement — Counterparty (TxDOT) Markup
Re: Redline Review of TxDOT Markup Against Original Draft and Negotiation Playbook

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We have reviewed the counterparty's markup (the "TxDOT Markup") of the Concession Agreement against our original draft, our internal negotiation playbook, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the deal-team correspondence that controls this engagement. We have cross-referenced the lender and surety letters and the financial model in assessing the commercial and risk impact of each deviation.

The TxDOT Markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  1. Indemnification cap reduction coupled with conversion of the basket from a
     true deductible to a tipping basket (Markup § __, touching Schedule 5.2).
  2. Expansion of the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition to carve out
     regulatory action of the kind at issue in this matter (Markup § __,
     intersecting Schedule 3.7).
  3. A shortened survival/limitation period for the core representations
     (Markup § __, contradicting Exhibit B survival matrix).

Risk ratings (defined in § IV): Deviation 1 is MEDIUM-HIGH and partially concedible; Deviation 2 is HIGH; Deviation 3 is CRITICAL and is a walk-away item under the controlling instruction.

Controlling instruction (deal correspondence, latest message): The client will concede the basket conversion but treats ANY reduction of the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages expressing the opposite priority are superseded and do not govern. The deal team's position must therefore hold the survival period at the Exhibit B matrix and reject the markup's limitation-period change without concession.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. SCOPE AND SOURCES REVIEWED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following operative records were reviewed in full:

  - Original draft of the Concession Agreement and negotiation playbook
    (firm-standard base materials).
  - Counterparty Markup (TxDOT) — deviation set.
  - Schedules and Exhibits, including Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory
    inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival
    matrix). Per the schedules, scheduled exceptions control over general
    statements in the base materials.
  - Deal correspondence — controlling latest instruction.
  - Lender and surety letters and the financial model, cross-referenced to
    quantify the commercial impact of each deviation on the concession
    financing and security package.

Note on misfiled materials: A document identified as "Unrelated correspondence —
administrative file 13" was located in the matter folder but expressly must not
be relied upon for this analysis. It has been excluded from this review.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. REDLINE DEVIATION ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
------------------------------------------------------------------

What the markup does: The markup (a) silently reduces the aggregate indemnification cap below the level in the original draft and (b) converts the basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket.

Cross-reference to schedules: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that would be silently shifted by the indemnification changes. Under the original draft, the deductible was a true dollar threshold that the indemnitor bore in full before any recovery; a tipping basket would instead expose the full amount once the threshold is crossed, effectively expanding the indemnitor's exposure for the band between the deductible and the cap. Combined with a reduced cap, the markup narrows seller-side protection and reallocates retained-liability risk onto the buyer while simultaneously lowering the ceiling on recoverable losses.

Cross-reference to financial model: The financial model's reserved-liability line and the deductibility timing assumptions are calibrated to a true deductible. Converting to a tipping basket accelerates and increases modeled exposure; the reduced cap alters the tail-risk allocation reflected in the model's downside scenario. The quantified delta should be reconciled against the model's reserved-liability forecast before finalizing any agreed cap.

Cross-reference to lender and surety letters: The lender letter conditions availability on the buyer retaining the benefit of the full indemnity cap and on scheduled retained liabilities (Schedule 5.2) being recoverable. The surety letter assumes the basket operates as a true deductible for purposes of the performance/security package. The markup's changes therefore implicate the comfort the lender and surety have relied on in sizing the facility and security.

Risk rating: MEDIUM-HIGH.

Controlling instruction impact: The client will concede the basket conversion. Accordingly, the tipping-basket structure may be accepted. The cap reduction, however, is a separate and uncompelled concession and should be resisted or traded only against a meaningful offset.

Recommended position: Concede the basket conversion as instructed, but counter the cap reduction to hold the cap at the original-draft level (and in any event above the financial-model-supported floor). Do not permit the cap reduction to extend to, or swallow, the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability recoveries.

DEVIATION 2 — MAE Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action
---------------------------------------------------

What the markup does: The markup expands the MAE definition to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Cross-reference to schedules: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs. The scheduled inquiries concern precisely the category of regulatory action the markup would carve out. Under the schedules' controlling rule, the scheduled exceptions narrow the relevant representations, so the carve-outs cannot be read in isolation; they must be reconciled against the disclosed inquiries so that the carve-out does not neutralize a disclosed, material regulatory risk.

Cross-reference to lender and surety letters: The lender and surety letters treat the pendency and possible outcome of the Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries as material contingencies that must remain squarely within the transaction's risk allocation. Excluding regulatory action from MAE would strip the buyer of its condition-to-closing protections and effectively shift the downside of the very disclosed matters onto the buyer post-closing.

Risk rating: HIGH.

Recommended position: Reject the carve-out as drafted. If the counterparty insists on an MAE carve-out for regulatory action, it must (i) expressly except the Schedule 3.7 disclosed inquiries and any proceeding arising from, related to, or anticipated by those matters; and (ii) preserve the buyer's ability to terminate or reprice if a Schedule 3.7 matter materially advances or deteriorates.

DEVIATION 3 — Shortened Survival / Limitation Period for Core Representations
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

What the markup does: The markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations relative to the original draft.

Cross-reference to schedules/exhibits: Exhibit B establishes the survival matrix for the core representations. The markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts Exhibit B. Because scheduled exhibits control over general statements in the base materials, the markup cannot simply override the Exhibit B matrix.

Cross-reference to financial model: The financial model assumes post-closing recovery of breach-of-representation losses over the survival windows in Exhibit B. A shortened survival window truncates the modeled recovery period and materially reduces the present value of the buyer's indemnity protection, realigning risk to the buyer's detriment without any pricing offset.

Cross-reference to lender and surety letters: Both the lender and surety letters are premised on the full Exhibit B survival matrix remaining in place; shortening survival undermines the security/recovery assumptions in those letters.

Risk rating: CRITICAL.

Controlling instruction impact: The client treats ANY reduction of the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue. This is a non-negotiable, do-not-concede item.

Recommended position: Reject the limitation-period reduction outright. Hold the survival matrix at Exhibit B. This point is a walk-away item; do not trade it or substitute any shorter survival window.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. RISK-RATING FRAMEWORK
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  CRITICAL      — Non-negotiable; client-directed walk-away if not resolved to
                  the original position. No concession authority.
  HIGH          — Material adverse to client's economic/risk position; require
                  escalation and meaningful compensating terms before accepting.
  MEDIUM-HIGH   — Concedible in part where a controlling instruction compels
                  concession, but only up to the stated limit and only for
                  value.
  MEDIUM/LOW    — Administrative or minor; accept or resolve in ordinary course.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
V. CROSS-REFERENCE SUMMARY (MARKUP v. PLAYBOOK, SCHEDULES, LENDER/ SURETY, MODEL)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Deviation | Original Position        | Markup Change                | Cross-Reference                     | Risk     | Recommended Action
----------|--------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------------------------|----------|--------------------
Indem. cap/basket | Full cap; true deductible | Cap reduced; tipping basket | Sch 5.2; financial model; lender/surety | MEDIUM-HIGH | Concede basket; counter cap
MAE carve-outs    | No regulatory carve-out  | Reg. action carve-out added | Sch 3.7; lender/surety               | HIGH     | Reject/carve back disclosed matters
Survival period   | Exhibit B matrix         | Survival shortened          | Exhibit B; model; lender/surety      | CRITICAL | Reject — walk-away item

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. COUNTER-PROPOSAL LANGUAGE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

COUNTER TO DEVIATION 1 (Indemnification Cap and Basket):

"Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in the Concession Agreement as
marked by [TxDOT], (i) the indemnification cap shall remain at the amount set
forth in the original draft and shall not be reduced, and (ii) in the event the
parties agree to a tipping basket, [Buyer] shall continue to be entitled, on a
first-dollar basis, to recover all Retained Liabilities described in Schedule
5.2 and such recovery shall not be applied against, or limited by, the agreed
